docs.text: David Karl Hatchett Portfolio Hi, I’m David. I've been working as a data professional since 2012. I'm currently a Principal Data Analyst working in the banking Industry. I've spent many years building analytics solutions to help businesses make data-driven decisions. I have expertise in figuring out how data works and how to produce usable, insightful datasets, metrics, models, and visualizations. Contact: E-mail: dkh1871@gmail.com Technical Skills Data & Analytics: ETL, Data cleaning, Data analysis, Data visualization, Data storytelling, Data engineering, Data mining, Data modeling, Data governance, Metric development, Feature preparation Database: SQL Server, Snowflake, SQLite, Teradata Programming Languages: Python, SQL, VBA Python ecosystem: pandas, PyTorch, sklearn, Matplotlib, Conda Visualizations: Tableau Distributed Computing (Foundational): Spark, YARN, HDFS, Hive, Hbase, Nifi, Kafka, Solr Projects ADHD Diagnoses in Children Post COVID-19 This project is about investigating the ADHD diagnosis rates in children pre- and post-COVID-19. This project was about performing statistical analysis and practicing Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) techniques. The idea for this project was spurred by the medication shortages of ADHD treatments that have occurred since the pandemic. Board Game Data Cleaning and Loading Foucs on cleaning and loading data taken from Kaggle, but orginally from BoardGameGeek.com. The data is processed and loaded into an SQLite database. It also uses a multiprocessing approach to process the data. Board Game Ownership Prediction Model This is a project based on the Board Game Data Cleaning and Loading project. It extracts data from the SQLite database and builds a model to predict board game ownership. Board Game Recommendation Model This project explores the creation of a recommendation model using neural collaborative filtering(NCF) like architectures from users' reviews of board games. This project focused on practicing deep learning with PyTorch. Board Game User Classification This was an attempt to create user segmentation based on board game data. While I'm not going to pursue the project further, it still show skills in the use of clustering and machine learning techniques. Child Care Visualization In this project, I intended to work for an Illinois-based Charity focused on Child Care. I processed the data and created a dashboard, deck, and infographic. While I do have some training in design, it is not my primary focus, so there may be a way to superficially surface the mediums. The primary focus was on selecting good graphs to convey the needed information. Distributed Data Processing Project A project that focuses on the fundamentals of distributed data processing. An end-to-end machine learning pipeline is built and tested. Enity Matching POC Testing if it is possible to use HDBSCAN to cluster entities from poorly enter user data on Business. Heart Disease Model Testing Working with a dataset created on Kaggle to test three different classification models and see how well the models perform. Video Game Completion and Speed Run Times The primary purpose of this project was to practice various data wrangling techniques across different sources and to produce a coherent final output. The code in this report will ingest and process data from a flat file, scrape data from a website, and finalize data from a REST API. The code in the repo provides a fundamental understanding of ETL, Data cleaning, and Python skills.

docs.text: Distributed Data Processing Project Overview This project is the capstone for a graduate distributed systems course covering the Hadoop/Spark big data ecosystem. The goal was to build an end-to-end machine learning pipeline. The focus of this project was the pipeline and the tools used, not the ML model being run. Because of this, I chose a simple dataset from Kaggle. Technologies used: Google Cloud Platform (Compute Engine) Docker / Docker Compose Apache NiFi HDFS Hive Spark (PySpark) HBase YARN Environment This project ran a single Compute Engine VM created on Google Cloud. The machine had 4 CPUs and 16 GB of RAM. All applications ran on the same machine via Docker; as one might note, the available resources are insufficient to run all services simultaneously. To resolve this issue, services were brought up and down as needed. Pipeline Walkthrough 1. NiFi Ingestion into HDFS The flow used three NiFi processors: InvokeHTTP to pull the source data from GitHub, UpdateAttribute to rewrite the output filename, and PutHDFS to land the result in HDFS. 2. Hive Managed Table Loaded the ingested data into a Hive-managed table. At this point in the process, I didn’t see the need to transform the data extensively, as this was a one-off. In a normal pipeline, we would want to insert some data quality checks at this point to ensure the ingested file meets expected standards. 3. Environment Setup Across Nodes One of the benefits of Spark is that work can be split and completed by any number of workers. The following setup was performed to ensure all workers have access to the same Python packages and configuration. We could improve by updating the underlying image used to create the workers to include the needed configuration. 4. HBase Table for Model Metrics Created an HBase table to hold and track model run metrics. I designed the row key ( model_name_datetimestamp ) to be a combination of the model name and the run's date and time stamp. I chose this row key so that the same model run would be stored together, while different runs could be split across shards. 5. PySpark Model Training Below is the logistic regression model run as part of the project. Each run is stored in the table created in the previous step with the following fields: accuracy, weighted precision, and weighted recall in HBase. from pyspark.sql import SparkSession from pyspark.ml.feature import VectorAssembler from pyspark.ml.classification import LogisticRegression from pyspark.ml.evaluation import BinaryClassificationEvaluator import happybase from datetime import datetime now = datetime.now() run_name = f'personality_prediction_{now.strftime("%Y%m%d%H%M%S")}' # Function to write data to HBase inside each partition def write_to_hbase_partition(partition): connection = happybase.Connection('master') connection.open() table = connection.table('model_metrics') for row in partition: row_key, column, value = row table.put(row_key, {column: value}) connection.close() spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("personality_prediction").enableHiveSupport().getOrCreate() df = spark.sql(""" SELECT time_spent_alone, CASE WHEN stage_fear = 'Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS stage_fear, social_event_attendance, going_outside, CASE WHEN drained_after_socializing = 'Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS drained_after_socializing, friends_circle_size, post_frequency, CASE WHEN class = 'Introvert' THEN 0 WHEN class = 'Extrovert' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END AS class FROM personality """) assembler = VectorAssembler( inputCols=["time_spent_alone", "stage_fear", "social_event_attendance", "going_outside", "drained_after_socializing", "friends_circle_size", "post_frequency"], outputCol="features", handleInvalid="skip" ) final_df = assembler.transform(df).select("features", "class") train_data, test_data = final_df.randomSplit([0.8, 0.2]) lr = LogisticRegression(featuresCol="features", labelCol="class", maxIter=10, regParam=0.01, threshold=0.8, family="binomial") model = lr.fit(train_data) test_results = model.evaluate(test_data) data = [ (run_name, 'mm:accuracy', str(test_results.accuracy)), (run_name, 'mm:weightedPrecision', str(test_results.weightedPrecision)), (run_name, 'mm:weightedRecall', str(test_results.weightedRecall)), ] rdd = spark.sparkContext.parallelize(data) rdd.foreachPartition(write_to_hbase_partition) spark.stop() 6. Verify Results in HBase Limitations This pipeline lacks data quality and validation layers, as expected, since this project's focus is on setting up and running the pipeline. Without these layers, an upstream issue would cause the whole pipeline to fail. These are important layers to add if I were to convert the pipeline into production.
